title: Equilibrium compression calculation
description: Essential Criteria: Student correctly calculates the spring compression at equilibrium using l₁ = m_A g / k.

title: Height from ground
description: Essential Criteria: Student correctly computes the height h = natural length - l₁, yielding 8 cm.

title: Maximum compression relation
description: Important Criteria: Student recognizes that maximum downward compression is twice the equilibrium compression (l₂ = 2l₁) due to SHM symmetry.

title: Maximum pressure calculation
description: Essential Criteria: Student correctly calculates maximum pressure using N = m_B g + k l₂, yielding 4 N.

title: Spring force work calculation
description: Essential Criteria: Student correctly computes work done by spring force using W = (k l₁ + k l₂)/2 × l₁, yielding 0.03 J.

title: Unit consistency
description: Important Criteria: Student converts masses to kg and lengths to m to maintain consistent SI units in calculations.

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important Criteria: Student applies Newton's laws correctly to analyze forces on objects A and B at different positions.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall Criteria: Student incorrectly assigns positive sign to spring force work when it's actually negative (spring does negative work as A moves downward).

title: Ignoring B's mass in pressure
description: Pitfall Criteria: Student omits m_B g term when calculating maximum pressure on ground, using only k l₂.

title: Confusing compression signs
description: Pitfall Criteria: Student treats compression as negative displacement or misinterprets the direction of spring force.
